verdict.rationale: Kong AI Gateway calculates a provider-matching cost for every LLM request. It records cost alongside model details in standardized logs that aggregate usage analytics across providers, and it documents tracking costs across teams and per-consumer spend and chargeback. However, the docs never show a single view that breaks spend down by model, key, team, and user; the Konnect analytics citation lists requests, tokens, errors, and latency but not cost. missing for 10: explicit per-key and per-user spend breakdown documentation, a documented unified cost dashboard in Konnect (rather than logs or OTel export to other tools), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can track spend per model, key, team, or user across all providers in one place

citations.quote: AI Gateway calculates that figure for every request to a large language model (LLM) provider, matching what the provider actually bills.
AI Gateway logs capture detailed information about the request and response payloads, token usage, model details, latency, and cost metrics.
facilitating the aggregation of AI usage analytics across various providers
budget enforcement, per-consumer spend limits, and chargeback all depend on an accurate cost figure for each request
